text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan will face chemical trade sanctions for not ratifying the chemical weapons convention which comes into force on Monday (April 29).
- A ruling party member of the Punjab provincial Assembly Saeedul Haq Dogar was arrested on Sunday for sheltering proclaimed offenders and possessing illicit weapons.

- The decision to privatise Karachi Electric Supply Corp in the current year has posed a serious challenge to the state-run Privatisation Commission as the company's accumulative liabilities are estimated at 15 billion rupees.
- The government has strongly denied reports of an anticipated sugar crisis in the country.
- Leaders of 14 political parties and groups agreed to enter an alliance to provide an alternative leadership to the nation.

- The government has set up a four-member committee to look into state-run Water and Power Development Authority's power agreements with the private sector by the previous government at exorbitant rates.
- Sindh Chief Minister Liaquat Jatoi has said a plan has been prepared to revive the Nooriabad Industrial Estate to improve agro-based industries.
- A plan to link Pakistan with war-torn Afghanistan by rail is in the offing.

- Police have arrested the leaders of the militant Sunni Moslem organisation, Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan, including its president and former provincial minister Sheikh Hakim Ali and its general secretary Muhammad Yousaf.
